add.title: Other National S&T Missions and Strategies – Vigyan Dhara, Geospatial Policy, Nuclear and Mineral Missions
add.md:
# Other National S&T Missions and Strategies
- **Vigyan Dhara (DST):** Union Cabinet approved on **24 Aug 2024**; **merged three DST umbrella schemes** into one **central sector** scheme.
  - Three components: **S&T institutional and human capacity building**; **research and development**; **innovation, technology development and deployment**.
  - Outlay about **₹10,579 crore** for **2021-22 to 2025-26** (15th Finance Commission period); its R&D component follows **ANRF** guidelines.
- **Geospatial Guidelines (Feb 2021):** **DST** deregulated the collection and use of geospatial data and maps by Indian entities; no prior approval needed.
- **National Geospatial Policy 2022:** notified by **DST** in **Dec 2022**; replaces the **National Map Policy 2005** approach.
  - Apex body: **Geospatial Data Promotion and Development Committee (GDPDC)**, which absorbs the **National Spatial Data Committee (2006)** and the 2021 GDPDC.
  - Goals for **2035**: high-resolution topographic survey, **digital twins of major cities**, mapping of underground infrastructure, bathymetric data for the Blue Economy.
- **National Geospatial Mission:** announced in the **Union Budget 2025-26**; develops foundational geospatial infrastructure and data, uses **PM Gati Shakti**, and modernises land records and urban planning.
- **Nuclear Energy Mission:** **Union Budget 2025-26**; **₹20,000 crore** for R&D on **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs)**; at least **five indigenous SMRs operational by 2033**.
  - Part of the **100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047** goal. BARC is developing **Bharat Small Reactors** and Bharat Small Modular Reactors. The **SHANTI Act 2025** opened the sector to private players.
- **National Critical Mineral Mission:** approved **29 Jan 2025**; **₹34,300 crore** over seven years (₹16,300 crore Central outlay + ₹18,000 crore from PSUs). It covers exploration, overseas assets and recycling of lithium, REEs and similar minerals.
- **Mission Mausam (MoES):** approved **Sep 2024**; **₹2,000 crore** for two years; launched **14 Jan 2025**, IMD's 150th foundation day. Run by **IMD, IITM Pune and NCMRWF**.
- **Already covered above:** NSM (2015), NM-ICPS (2018), NQM (2023), IndiaAI (2024), BioE3 (2024), ISM, Deep Ocean Mission, NGHM (2023).
- **AP angle:** **Amaravati Quantum Valley** (NQM), **IISER Tirupati TIH** on positioning and precision technologies (NM-ICPS); **Kovvada** is the AP nuclear site and SMRs widen the options.
> Trap: Vigyan Dhara is a DST merger scheme, not an ANRF fund. The Geospatial Policy is DST's, not ISRO's. The Nuclear Energy Mission is about SMRs, not the PFBR.
~~ Sources: PIB 24 Aug 2024 (Vigyan Dhara); Drishti IAS / Vajiram (National Geospatial Policy 2022); World Nuclear News and PIB (Budget 2025 Nuclear Energy Mission); app notes 5:17, 5:70, 6:58

add.title: Major Terrestrial Ecosystems – Forest, Grassland, Desert and Tundra Biomes
add.md:
# Major Terrestrial Ecosystems (Biomes)
- **Biome:** a large terrestrial community shaped mainly by **temperature and rainfall**. Its dominant vegetation gives it its name.
- **Tropical rainforest:** near the equator; rain **above 200 cm**, hot all year; multi-layered canopy, epiphytes, lianas.
  - Holds the **highest species richness** on land; soils are **poor (laterite)** because decay and nutrient uptake are fast.
  - India: **Western Ghats, North-East, Andaman & Nicobar** (tropical wet evergreen).
- **Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forest:** trees shed leaves in the dry season; **teak, sal**.
  - **Tropical dry deciduous** is India's **most extensive forest type group** (ISFR). AP: Nallamala and Seshachalam dry deciduous forests (red sanders in Seshachalam).
- **Temperate deciduous and temperate grassland:** four distinct seasons. Grasslands are the **prairies, steppes, pampas, veld and downs**; they have deep fertile soils (chernozem) and are "granaries of the world".
- **Savanna:** tropical grassland with scattered trees and a long dry season; Africa (Serengeti). In India, the **terai grasslands** have savanna-like features.
- **Taiga (boreal coniferous forest):** about 50°–70° N; **conifers (spruce, fir, pine)** with needle leaves; long cold winters; **acidic podzol** soils with thick litter. It is the **largest land biome** by area.
- **Tundra:** beyond the treeline (Arctic) or high on mountains (alpine). **Permafrost**, a very short growing season, **mosses, lichens and sedges**, no trees; reindeer and musk ox. It has the **lowest productivity** of the land biomes.
- **Desert:** rain **below 25 cm**. Hot deserts are the **Thar and Sahara**; cold deserts are **Ladakh, Spiti and Gobi**.
  - Plants are **xerophytes**: thick cuticle, sunken stomata, CAM photosynthesis, deep roots.
- **Mountain (montane) ecosystems:** vegetation zones change with altitude. **Shola–grassland mosaic** occurs in the Nilgiris and Anamalai.
- **Man-made ecosystems:** croplands, plantations, gardens, aquaria and cities. They have **low diversity and need energy subsidies**.
- **India's forests (ISFR 2023, released Dec 2024):** forest cover **7,15,343 sq km = 21.76%** of area; with tree cover, **25.17%**. **Champion and Seth (1968)** classify India's forests into **16 type groups**.
> Exam angle: match a biome to its climate, soil or plant (taiga = conifers + podzol; tundra = permafrost + lichens; rainforest = richest but poor soil). Trap: savanna is a tropical grassland, steppe is temperate.
~~ Sources: NCERT Biology XII Ch.12-13 and Fundamentals of Physical Geography; ISFR 2023 (FSI, PIB Dec 2024); Shankar Environment (biomes); app notes 5:82
